$comment: T_TEST.8 — deliberate deviations from axe's defaults, each with the reason
it is deliberate. A rule belongs here only when somebody can say why the
check does not apply to this page; 'it was failing' is not a reason, it is
the finding. Anything not listed runs, and a violation fails the suite.
`tags` decides what is checked at all: the WCAG 2.2 AA tags, minus the two
colour rules below. What remains is the part of accessibility that is a bug
when it fails — an unnamed control, a broken list, a field with no label —
and none of it has an opinion about how the product looks.

disabled.why: Owner's decision, 2026-08-03. The muted scale is built from navy at 20–60% opacity, and most of it sits under 4.5:1 on light surfaces. Raising it to AA was tried and reverted: replacing the ramp with a solid token flattened the hierarchy the landing depends on, and the page stopped looking like the thing it was designed to be. The palette is a product decision and it is made deliberately, not by a test. Consequence written down rather than hidden: Vimana does not meet WCAG 2.2 AA on text contrast, and any claim to the contrary is a §9.1 violation — see DESIGNGUIDELINES §6.

Follows from the rule above. It fires when a link inside a paragraph is distinguished from the surrounding text by colour alone, and the fix is either a permanent underline or a contrast ratio between the two colours — both are the same visual decision, and it was made the same way.
Best-practice rule (not WCAG AA) that wants every node inside a landmark. It is out of scope for the tags above and is listed only so nobody re-adds it as if it were a level-AA requirement.

$pending: Nothing is parked here. When a violation is accepted temporarily rather
than fixed, it goes in this list with a task id and a date — separate from
`disabled`, because 'we decided this does not apply' and 'we have not got
to it yet' are different statements and must not look the same.
